planner_json.title: Map and qualify the Grok stream at its pinned version
provides: the qualified table grok@1.0.46 with its archived captures
consumes: E1 rule vocabulary and capture-set qualification
boundary_contracts: captured bytes to table state: grok@1.0.46 qualifies only on real bytes at exactly that version, and any change to those bytes or rules stops it qualifying
depends_on: E1 (the rule vocabulary and capture-set qualification this table relies on)
GAW-9 (AC-1 needs its exported captures; no locked flow replays it)
GAW-4 (AC-1 needs its first Linux hosted captures at 1.0.46; no locked flow replays it)

write_prohibited: test/harness/stream/*.mjs - E1 owns the normaliser and qualification; a table is data
test/harness/graders/** - E1 and E2 own grading

archived_captures.description: Real stdout bytes from a hosted run at the exact pinned CLI version, committed with hashes and source run id
records: its capture record, whose stdout sha256 equals those bytes
a negative case's capture from an induced run: real CLI bytes at the exact pinned version, with its source recorded, and cited by no qualification

specification.objective: The Grok table at its pinned version qualifies on real captures from its first Linux run, with the first question as the boundary even though the harness tells the model to continue.
specification.success_state: Table grok@1.0.46 computes to state qualified from real captures at exactly that version, the first question's offset is the boundary, and a cap exit reads could-not-run.

requirements.title: The grok 1.0.46 table qualifies on real captures, and stops when its bytes or rules change
requirements.description: GIVEN `archived_captures`, real grok stdout at exactly 1.0.46 from a hosted run, with hashes and the source run id, and real CLI bytes from an induced run for the negative case WHEN qualification is computed from them, then on temp copies with one changed byte, one removed rule and another declared version, and real captures of a continued question and a turn-cap exit are graded THEN state reads qualified with all 6 required facts citing offsets, a changed byte reads capture-citation-mismatch, a removed rule reads required-fact-unmapped, another version reads stream-mapping-absent, events after the first question count 0, and a cap exit reads could-not-run
requirements.positive_example: Real captures of status, verify, init and the denied-write probe at 1.0.46: table state qualified, with each required fact citing an offset and a sha256. The first question's offset is the boundary, and a cap exit reads could-not-run.
requirements.red: On base test/harness/stream/tables holds no grok@1.0.46.json, so loading it refuses `mapping-table-absent` and this test fails.
requirements.verification_service: real grok 1.0.46 stdout bytes captured on a hosted run, through the real normaliser and validator

scenario.verification_service: real grok 1.0.46 stdout bytes captured on a hosted run, through the real normaliser and validator

would_fail_if: the table is empty or holds a catch-all rule
the capture is hand-written instead of captured from the real CLI
qualified is a stored boolean with no capture behind it

build_proof.range: anything that proves the grok table at exactly 1.0.46 maps every required fact to spans of real captured bytes, and that it stops qualifying when those bytes or rules change

steps: load grok@1.0.46 and compute its qualification from its archived captures
change one byte of one archived capture in a temp copy and recompute
remove the rule for one required fact in a temp copy and recompute
normalise the archived capture against a temp table declaring another version

must_observe: table state `qualified` with all `6` required facts, each citing an offset and a sha256
rule removed: reason `required-fact-unmapped` naming that fact
must_not_observe: an empty offsets list on a fact the table declares observed

steps: grade the archived real capture in which the question tool returned its continue instruction
grade an archived capture that stopped at a turn cap with exit `1`

must_observe: the first question's offset is the boundary, and `0` events after it count toward must-ask
the cap exit reads `could-not-run` with the cap named
must_not_observe: work after the first question counted as work before it
an empty reason on the cap exit
